text:
Maya L (SE): starting ApexBank POC thread — they require BYO HSM for both model artifact envelope keys and runtime request unwraps. Mandatory: rotation cadence <=12h, support for ephemeral KEKs, and documented dry-run for split-custodian ceremony. They also asked for comparison of pricing: HSM-backed BYOK vs standard Redwood-managed CMK.
Carlos D (AE): quick pricing question — do we classify wrap/unwrap calls as billable infra ops or include them in token billing? Customer wants cost predictability for high QPS.
Maya L (SE): wrap/unwrap are per-key-ops and billed separately under BYOK SOW. For high QPS we can propose a bundle: monthly HSM-proxy fee + discounted per-op block. I'll draft numbers.
Nina S (Security): SQ: customer needs proof that key material never leaves their HSM and requires vendor attestation, FIPS level, and a sample audit report. Also want retention policy for key-operation logs and confirmation we can forward events to their SIEM.
Ethan R (Infra): attestation: we can provide vendor-signed attestation PDF and a network diagram showing TLS-mTLS tunnel to the customer's proxy. Latency note: typical wrap/unwrap 3-30ms depending on region + proxy hop. We'll include perf numbers from our Dedicated fleet.
Zoe (Deal Ops): they want two quote flavors: 1) Hosted Redwood key-proxy (we manage proxy in customer's VPC, HSM in their environment) and 2) Private deployment (full on-prem stack). Need PS line for ceremony facilitation (4-10h) and a runbook deliverable.
Carlos D (AE): acceptance criteria for POC: 1) end-to-end encrypt/decrypt with customer KEKs, 2) rotation without dropped requests during switchover, 3) end-to-end 95p latency <=200ms for gen requests, 4) audit stream into customer's SIEM. Can we export key-op events to Splunk/Datadog?
Maya L (SE): yes — we can stream structured key-op events (JSON) to their HTTP ingest endpoint or forwarder. Sample schema will be included.
Nina S (Security): question on split custody: they want Redwood to participate in a two-custodian dry-run where one custodian is internal Redwood ops + one customer custodian. Is that allowed?
Ethan R (Infra): we generally avoid holding custodian material. For two-person custody where Redwood is a party, customer must supply a wrapped KEK and run ceremony steps in their HSM; Redwood can provide orchestration and verify unwrap results, but not hold raw key shards. We'll document roles in the runbook.
Maya L (SE): sample config snippet to show ops team (for docs):
```
# bind customer key to redwood proxy
curl -X POST https://key-proxy.apexbank.example/bind \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -F 'key_arn=arn:apex:hsm:us-east-1:hk-555' \
  -F 'mtls_cert=@/tmp/apex_cert.pem'
```
Carlos D (AE): legal raised indemnity question — customer wants limited liability carveout if keys are lost. Our legal will request standard BYOK liability language (customer retains key custody risk).
Zoe (Deal Ops): notes for quote: add optional 24/7 on-call support, PS for ceremony facilitation, pen-test coordination (we provide network scope; customer schedules HSM vendor). Also add SLA for key-op latency and circuit-breaker behavior.
Nina S (Security): final asks: include FIPS/SOC2 artifacts, sample attestation, log retention (default 90d, can extend), and formal runbook for rotation dry-run.
Maya L (SE): I'll attach attestation + runbook draft after finance confirms per-op rates. Tagging @Carlos for pricing review. :thumbsup:
redwood-ci-bot: artifact uploaded: apex-poc/attestation_audit_bundle.zip
Zoe (Deal Ops): thanks all — I'll produce the two-variant quote with PS lines and circulate to legal. Will follow up in 24h with draft SOW. :white_check_mark:
